app.title: Telescope frame triage before stacking
app.summary: The person sees every frame from one observing session as a small image in a grid, with its quality numbers underneath, beside a large view of the current frame and its full details. They step through the frames with the arrow keys and keep or reject each one, picking a reason from a short numbered list when they reject, and the view moves on to the next frame. They can reorder the grid by a quality number to bring the worst frames together and switch the display stretch to judge faint detail. A running tally shows how many frames are kept, their total exposure against a target and the rejections by reason, and the result is exported as a list of kept files and a table of every decision.

task.text: Decide which frames of a session to keep for stacking, record why each rejected frame was dropped, and check that enough exposure is left.

data.text: A set of image frames of the same field taken over one session, each with computed quality numbers (sharpness, elongation, background, detected source count), a time stamp, and a keep or reject decision with a reason from a fixed list.
data.item: one exposure frame of the same field, with its quality numbers and decision

stage.text: after the data is taken, before combining the frames

mechanism.text: A thumbnail grid of every frame sits beside a large viewer and fact list for the current one; arrow keys move through the grid in its current sort order, k and r keep or reject, a reject waits for a numbered reason, and each decision advances to the next frame while the header tally updates.

workflow.name: triage a collection one item at a time

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Every frame of the night is a thumbnail in a grid with its FWHM, sky background and number of stars detected underneath, its decision as text, rejected frames dimmed and the current one outlined.

steps.step: order the items by a quality measure
steps.here: A sort menu reorders the grid, and the order the keys step through, by time taken, FWHM sharpest first, background darkest first or most stars detected, so a stretch of bad seeing sits together.

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: Left and right arrows move one frame in the current order, up and down move a whole grid row, a click on a thumbnail jumps to it, and every decision moves on to the next frame.

The current frame is drawn large with its file name, position in the order, UT start, exposure, FWHM, elongation, background, stars detected and decision; an asinh or linear stretch repaints every frame so faint stars can be judged.

steps.step: decide keep or drop for each item, with a reason
steps.here: k keeps a frame; r rejects it and waits for a numbered reason, 1 to 4 for trail, cloud, blur or other, which can also be pressed directly or clicked as buttons.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: The header counts frames kept, rejected and not decided, totals the kept exposure in minutes against an editable target with how many more frames are needed, and breaks the rejections down by reason.

One button downloads the kept file names one per line for the stacking script; another downloads a CSV of every frame with its time, exposure, FWHM, elongation, background, star count, decision and reason.

distinctive: Kept exposure is totalled against an editable target, and the header says how many more frames would reach it, so the person knows whether enough is left to stack.
Rejections are counted by reason in the header, the breakdown a night report asks for.
A display stretch switch between asinh and linear repaints every frame so faint sources can be judged, not only bright ones.
Every frame shows the same patch of sky, so the quality numbers under each thumbnail compare directly and sorting by one brings a bad stretch of the session together.
The kept list is exported as bare file names, one per line, ready to feed straight into the next processing script.
